newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
TALKS ON TO DEFUSE CRISIS

Notwithstanding the Congress party chief's confidence that the ruling United Front would finally back them to form the government, party leaders saw an answer to the political stalemate in former prime minister V.P. Singh's call for talks between the two sides. Congress circles did not expect any immediate breakthrough in the talks until it became clear to the party after the vote of confidence that, other than a coalition, there was no way fresh polls could be avoided or the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) prevented from gaining power.
Indian Express
ADAMANT PRIME MINISTER RATTLES PARTNERS

Even as Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda reiterated his intention not to step down before the vote of confidence, pressure mounted from within the ruling United Front (UF) to reach a compromise with the Congress. Former prime minister V.P. Singh was of the opinion that Tamil Maanila Congress chief Moopanar should be elected as the leader of the UF to clear the way for a rapprochement with the Congress.
The Times Of India
POLITICAL ECLIPSE MAY NOT CAST ITS SHADOW ON BUDGET

Prospects for the passage of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget in parliament brightened. The government and sections of industry began concerted efforts towards salvaging the budget from the present political turmoil. A move was afoot to get the budget passed in the lower house with the support of all parties before the government faced the confidence vote by April 11. The move received positive response from the Congress chief who indicated the party was willing to help pass the bill.
The Economic Times
SUPPORT PRICE FOR WHEAT HIKED

The government increased the minimum support price for wheat from 415 rupees to 475 rupees per quintal. The increase would come through a central government bonus. The government also decided to provide an additional seven-billion-rupee subsidy for the targeted public distribution system over and above the budgetary provisions.
EXTERNAL COMMERCIAL BORROWING NORMS EASED

External commercial borrowing (ECB) norms for corporates, lending institutions and the infrastructure sector were relaxed with immediate effect. Corporate borrowers would be able to raise external debt of 10-year and 20-year maturities without any end-use restrictions, provided the money was not used in the stock markets or real estate. The cap on 10-year debt was fixed at $100 million, while that for 20-year debt at $200 million.
GOVERNMENT OFFER FAILS TO WOO TRUCKERS

The government decided to defer the proposed hike in insurance premium rates for commercial vehicles to pacify striking truck operators. However, the truckers were still to fall in line and the movement of goods across the country remained disrupted. The Tariff Advisory Committee would hold further discussions with the representatives of truck operators regarding new rates to be applied to commercial vehicles.
Financial Express
EXCHANGE RATE PROFIT NORMS REJECTED

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would not allow commercial banks to show profits arising out of exchange rate fluctuations in the profit and loss account in 1996/97 (April-March). RBI had refused to accept the accounting norms for valuation of foreign exchange positions and booking of exchange profits and losses prescribed by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI).
IOC TURNOVER MAY RISE TO 530 BLN RUPEES IN 1996/97

Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), the only Indian company to figure in the Fortune 500 list, was likely to report 530 billion rupees in turnover during 1996/97 (April-March). This was about 14 percent higher than the previous year's figure. The state-owned oil major, with a 55 percent market share, reported a turnover of 464.47 billion rupees in 1995/96. With this performance, IOC would become the first company in the country's corporate history to achieve the 500 billion rupee turnover mark.
CORPORATES SEE POLITICAL FLUX AS A PASSING CLOUD

The domestic corporate sector, which was labouring under a prolonged economic slowdown even before the United Front (UF) government came to power, may not alter its long-term investment plans due to the sudden turn in the political scenario. The corporate sector, which put up an unimpressive show due to a dull capital market and high interest rates, was gradually gaining confidence in the UF government after it presented a turnaround budget aimed at the revival of the economy.
Business Standard
NEW ACT TO REDFINE INDUSTRIAL SICKNESS

The recast Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA) would redefine industrial sickness in terms of bankruptcy instead of erosion of net worth. The act would eliminate the role of an operating agency for framing the rehabilitation package for the sick industry. The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) would become a facilitator under the revamped act. The criterion to determine bankruptcy within a company would be four quarterly defaults on debt repayment in a two-year period.
The Observer
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX UP 66 POINTS

Stock prices staged a mild recovery as domestic financial institutions (FIs) and foreign institutional investors (FIIs) made substantial purchases at lower levels. The Bombay Stock Exchange Sensitive Index rose by 66.12 points and the NSE-50 index by 2.85. The Sensex opened on a weak note at 3,339.47 points and the selling pressure pushed it down to the intra-day low of 3,315.36. However, the local FIs and the FIIs started buying with the predetermined price limits. The index improved to a high of 3,438.27 to finally settle at 3,427.01.
Business Line
RAIL PROJECTS WORTH 11 BLN RUPEES CLEARED

The government cleared railway projects worth around 11 billion rupees proposed in the 1997/98 (April-March) rail budget. But no expenditures on these projects would actually be incurred until parliament approves the proposals in the budget. Two projects for Gujarat include construction of a new line costing over 2.45 billion and a project for doubling of line from Nerguhdi to Cuttack. The other two projects would be a new line from Salem to Karur and the gauge conversion on the Surendranagar-Bhavnagar-Pipai segment.
